articles.title: We tried 15 lotions over three weeks. Here’s which our testers loved – and which left them high and dry
articles.summary: From Jergens and Naturium to CeraVe and Eucerin, there’s a potion on this list that will keep every body soft and moisturized. The best facial cleansers in the US for every skin type, recommended by dermatologists.
body: Your skin is the largest organ on the body. Taking care of it can feel like a full-time job, especially if you struggle with anything from dryness and sun damage to psoriasis, not to mention allergies and hormone fluctuations over time. Picking the right lotion for your skin is crucial – and it’s much more of a health decision than many people realize.

Packaging, brand loyalty, fragrance or recommendations from your favorite influencers might factor into your decision. But when considering a lotion for long-term use, the best options are those that will actually benefit the skin.

To narrow down the choices, we assembled a group of five enthusiastic testers to test 15 lotions over the course of three weeks, and asked them about everything from scents to the design of the packaging. With their feedback, we compiled a comprehensive list of lotion ratings.

articles.title: ‘It gives Shein’: how did polyester become the world’s most-hated material?
articles.summary: Due to its ubiquity in fast fashion, gen Z are pushing back against the synthetic material and using it as an insult. In 2015, Kate Moss called an easyJet pilot a “basic bitch” and a catchy new insult meaning obvious and uncool hit the mainstream.
body: But its use as a figurative insult also echoes a literal backlash against polyester, now the most-produced synthetic fibre on the planet.

In gyms, the pilates princess aesthetic with its synthetic matching sets is waning while 1990s-style exercise gear is becoming fashionable once more as many lionize exercise garments displaying visible sweat – think Sylvester Stallone in Rocky, or John Travolta being sweatily hypnotized by Jamie Lee Curtis’s rocking pelvis in the 1985 movie Perfect.

Some of the pushback centres around polyester’s impact on the planet. Derived from fossil fuels, it does not biodegrade, and sheds microplastics when washed. Many anti-polyester influencers, however, talk about giving up the fabric in the same way they might talk about giving up sugar, sharing content with hashtags such as #naturalfibers, #antipolyester and #nontoxicclothing while posting videos of large shopping hauls of cotton and linen from Zara.
points: Due to its ubiquity in fast fashion, gen Z are pushing back against the synthetic material and using it as an insult.

articles.title: ‘I wanted to find the slowest fashion imaginable’: the woman growing her own dress
articles.summary: Looking for an alternative to fast fashion, Eve Ogden Schaub decided to create a garment from homegrown flax. From crop tops to shorts and brightly patterned dresses, many of today’s clothes are the result of fast fashion.
body: Eve Ogden Schaub is in the midst of a project to create a linen garment made from flax she is growing at home, documenting the process in videos shared on her Instagram account.
“I had this idea that I wanted to find the slowest fashion imaginable. And that’s when I had the idea I could grow a dress from seed in my back yard,” she says.

Schaub began the project in April 2025 when she turned a 600 sq ft vegetable garden in Vermont into a plot for growing flax. Having harvested the first crop, Schaub sowed and harvested a second. She is also learning to process the material in steps that would not sound amiss in a Grimms’ fairytale – sometimes enlisting family and friends to help.

“We retted it, which is a sort of decomposition process, and then you do breaking and scutching and hackling, and you have to spin and scour and then maybe dye your yarn,” she says, adding that she has yet to get to the latter step, but is growing indigo plants for the purpose.
points: Looking for an alternative to fast fashion, Eve Ogden Schaub decided to create a garment from homegrown flax.
From crop tops to shorts and brightly patterned dresses, many of today’s clothes are the result of fast fashion.

articles.title: The showgirl sisterhood: five former variety stars look back at their wild careers – in pictures
articles.summary: The ‘Golden girls of Eastbourne’ first crossed paths more than 50 years ago. They recall flammable feather head-dresses, wardrobe malfunctions and topping the bill over the Beatles.
body: I hear the Golden Girls of Eastbourne before I see them – hooting laughter leaking out of a house in the East Sussex seaside town. Inside, I find five energetic women in their 80s and 90s, sitting in a knick-knack-filled living room and talking over one another like teenagers.

Friends for more than half a century, the women met in rehearsals and aftershow parties while working as dancers, singers and comedy stooges in the 1960s and 70s. Their careers took them from cruise ships and panto to British seaside theatres, where they performed in sequin dresses, high-cut leotards and huge feather headdresses, sharing bills with the biggest stars of the day.
He decided to photograph them at the town’s Royal Hippodrome – a Victorian theatre where all the women performed when they were younger.

“It’s a beautiful theatre,” says former dancer and dance teacher Jenny Lawrenson, 83. Petite, with the voice of Mary Poppins and the impeccable posture of a lifelong ballet dancer, she says she remembers it better for another reason – its tilted stage: “You’re dancing uphill!”

articles.title: This Maximalist Wedding in Southern California Artfully Blended South Indian and Black American Traditions
articles.summary: For their wedding in Dana Point, Ramya Velury and Joseph Harris fused their cultural backgrounds for a multi-day celebration unfolding across four distinct events.
body: A few months before Ramya Velury met Joseph Harris, a clairvoyant told her she’d reconnect with a man who had already been in her orbit, and who was also a twin. “I didn’t know any twins at that time,” Ramya says, “but then I met Joe and his twin.”

It was 2022, and Joe was working remotely from his colleague Jenna Adler’s house. “Jenna’s mission in life during this time was to ‘find Joe a girlfriend,’” he laughs. Later in the evening, she proposed a question to the group: Who can we set Joe up with? Another friend suggested Ramya. About an hour later, she arrived. “After a knock on the door, in comes Ramya with a fresh face and as beautiful as ever,” Joe says, “although Ramya will tell you she looked like a glazed donut as she had just come from a facial.” Ramya sat down at the table of friends and jumped right into the conversation without hesitation. “From that moment, I was all in,” Joe says.
points: For their wedding in Dana Point, Ramya Velury and Joseph Harris fused their cultural backgrounds for a multi-day celebration unfolding across four distinct events.

articles.title: Sarah Jones Fell Out of Love With America. Her New Play Takes It to Counseling
articles.summary: “I knew I wasn’t the only one feeling disoriented and grief-stricken, and that by speaking up, I might help others who were lost or afraid in their own relationship to America realize they aren’t alone."
body: For much of my life, I was in one of those relationships that feels too good to be true, and I couldn’t let it go. As a writer and actress, I’ve always been great at projecting my magical versions of others onto them, so instead of scrutinizing some of the flags that were there from the beginning, I let myself believe in what has now become one of the biggest heartbreaks of my life.

But it didn’t start out that way—at first, I felt so lucky to be in the relationship that I basically pledged my allegiance to it daily. And I had plenty of reasons to feel so devoted. The love languages were there: acts of service, words of affirmation. I learned to count on all the promises I heard, that I would always have the best of everything, that there were people who would give anything to be in the position I was.

articles.title: What Would a ‘How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days’ Sequel Even Be About? 5 Predictions
articles.summary: “I want dating apps, I want ghosting, I want breadcrumbing, I want that thing where you arrange a drink with someone even though you really can’t be bothered and would rather be at home eating a posh lasagna for one.”
body: Another day, another millennial-nostalgia-baiting sequel to a classic late 1990s or early 2000s movie. This year alone we’ve had The Devil Wears Prada 2 and Practical Magic 2 —and now there are rumors of another afoot. Over the last week, it was reported that the 2003 rom-com How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, starring Kate Hudson and Matthew McConnaughey, may well be returning to screens for a part two.

In the original movie, Hudson plays Andie, a journalist writing an article about the most off-putting things women can do in relationships, while McConnaughey is Ben, an advertising exec who, for convoluted professional reasons, bets his colleagues that he can make any woman fall in love with him. Hijinks, as we know, very much ensue.
